title: PR thread lens — review heuristics & follow-ups
content:
Purpose: quick personal lens for scanning large PR threads fast and leaving high-signal followups. Use this as my one-page checklist before posting block/approve comments or handing off to SRE/QA.

High-level strategy:
- First 5 minutes: read the PR description, linked ticket(s), and the top-level files changed (focus on public APIs, config, and safety boundaries).
- Next 10 minutes: grep for behavior-changing lines (config defaults, feature flags, SQL/DB schema, RPC surface).
- Final 10–15 minutes: scan tests and CI config, then leave an action-prioritized comment list.

Quick commands I run:
- git fetch origin && git checkout -b tmp-review origin/PR_BRANCH_NAME
- git log --stat --first-parent origin/main..HEAD --name-only | sed -n '1,120p'  # quick changed files
- rg "TODO|FIXME|hack|tbd" --hidden -S || true
- git diff --unified=0 origin/main...HEAD | sed -n '1,240p'  # small hunks only

Red flags to escalate immediately:
- Hard-coded credentials or new secret file additions.
- Changes to inference runtime startup/coordination (leader election, graceful shutdown hooks).
- Database migrations without rollout/rollback plan.
- New sync paths on hot request path (could increase tail latency).
- Disabled or removed telemetry/metrics spans for critical flows.

Light-touch checklist (comments ranked by priority):
1) Safety/Risk (blocker if present): data leak, secret checkin, schema change without plan.
2) Behavioral change (must call out): default config changes, deprecated behavior removal.
3) Test coverage (required): unit + integration for any new logic; smoke e2e for infra changes.
4) Observability (optional but important): missing metrics/traces or counter increments for new code paths.
5) Rollout plan (nice-to-have): feature flag, canary steps, migration windows.
6) Perf considerations: new synchronous loops, O(N^2) patterns, allocation in hot loop.

Notes-to-self for comments phrasing: keep each comment short, include expected fix, and classify as [blocker]/[high]/[medium]/[low]. Example: "[high] default batch_size=1024 increases mem pressure — prefer 256 and add benchmark results."

Refactor ideas (scratch):
- Split infer/request_handler.go into handler + validator + telemetry decorators to reduce PR surface for future reviews.
- Consolidate repeated retry logic across retries/* into a single util with pluggable backoff policy.
- Introduce a small linterset for serving-runtime to catch allocations in hot loops.

Follow-ups to create after merge: (create tickets, assign owners)
- Add a perf regression benchmark for this endpoint (ticket: PERF-ctx-123).
- Postmortem template entry if rollout flapped (owner: Diego).
- Eval prompt-set to check quality change if model quantization flags were toggled.

Risk scoring (quick heuristic):
- Score 0–5 for each: safety, latency, correctness, observability, rollout complexity. Total >=12 -> require SRE + product sign-off.

Common nit templates to copy/paste:
- [nit] small rename suggestion for clarity: `xxx` -> `yyy`
- [style] follow the repo lint rules (run `make fmt && make lint`)
- [test] add a unit test for X and a small integration test for Y

Unresolved questions to ask the author:
- What backwards-compat guarantees are expected for this change?
- Any load-tested numbers for the new default config?
- Will this require infra changes (ASG/GPU type) for Dedicated customers?

My current open TODOs for this PR review:
- [ ] Add comment about default config memory
- [ ] Request benchmark artifacts from author
- [ ] Check that feature flag has telemetry gate
- [ ] Run CI locally for the integration test that failed once in CI

Back-of-envelope note: if the PR touches more than 8 directories and includes >500 lines of behavioral code, schedule a 30-minute pairing review with the author (screenshare) — quicker than chasing threads.

Last-minute heuristics:
- If the change is small but touches a lot of files, look for scaffolding/renames vs real logic.
- If tests were added but only happy-path, request a failing-path test.
- If author added a migration, ensure they included an idempotent/rollback plan.

Meta: keep this doc short and portable — copy relevant lines into PR comments, and then tidy up this scratchpad with final links & tickets when handing off to QA.
